verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:1]
notes: The quotation introduced here extends from Lev 4:2 through 5:13, and encompasses all the sin offering regulations. Compare the notes on Lev 1:1 above, and 5:14 and 6:1 [5:20 HT] below.

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：若有人在耶和华所吩咐不可行的甚么事上误犯了一件，
verses.en: “Tell the Israelites, ‘When a person sins by straying unintentionally[NOTE:1] from any of the Lord’s commandments which must not be violated, and violates any[NOTE:2] one of them[NOTE:3]—
notes: Heb “And a person, when he sins in straying.” The English translation of “by straying” (בִּשְׁגָגָה [bishgagah] literally, “in going astray; in making an error”) varies greatly, but almost all suggest that this term refers to sins that were committed by mistake or done not knowing that the particular act was sinful (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:228-29). See, e.g., LXX “involuntarily”; Tg. Onq. “by neglect”; KJV “through ignorance”; ASV, RSV, NJPS “unwittingly”; NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “unintentionally”; NAB, NEB “inadvertently”; NCV “by accident.” However, we know from Num 15:27-31 that committing a sin “by straying” is the opposite of committing a sin “defiantly” (i.e., בְּיַד רָמָה [beyad ramah] “with a raised hand,” v. 30). In the latter case the person, as it were, raises his fist in presumptuous defiance against the Lord. Thus, he “blasphemes” the Lord and has “despised” his word, for which he should be “cut off from among his people” (Num 15:30-31). One could not bring an offering for such a sin. The expression here in Lev 4:2 combines “by straying” with the preposition “from” which fits naturally with “straying” (i.e., “straying from” the Lord’s commandments). For sins committed “by straying” from the commandments (Lev 4 throughout) or other types of transgressions (Lev 5:1-6) there was indeed forgiveness available through the sin offering. See R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:94-95.
This is an emphatic use of the preposition מִן (min; see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 56-57, §325).

The “when” clause (כִּי, ki) breaks off here before its resolution, thus creating an open-ended introduction to the following subsections, which are introduced by “if” (אִם [ʾim] vv. 3, 13, 27, 32). Also, the last part of the verse reads literally, “which must not be done and does from one from them.”
verses.commentary:
4:2

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NIV
"sins unintentionally"

TEV
"without intending to"

NJB, REB
"inadvertently"

JPSOA, ASV
"unwittingly"

Peshitta, KJV
"unwillingly"

Targum Onkelos
"by neglect"

This word "unintentionally" (BDB 993) shows a significant aspect of the ancient covenant. What
follows is a discussion of the sin offerings, the guilt offering (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS
OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST V. D. and E. at Lev. 1:3). To some extent the sins that are involved in the guilt offerings
are intentional sins. However, generally it was understood that if a person wilfully rebelled against YHWH's covenant,
there was no sacrifice available for him (cf. Num. 15:27; Lev. 5:15; Ps. 51:16-17). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: UNINTENTIONAL SINS.

▣ "a person" This is the term nephesh (BDB 659, cf. Lev. 4:2,27; 5:1,2,4,15,17,21), which denotes a
person or living animal. See full note online at Ezek. 18:4.

▣ "commanded" This term (BDB 846) is one of several words used to describe YHWH's covenant
requirements. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "commits any of them" This broad statement is repeated in Deut. 27:26 and Gal. 3:10. Perfect
obedience is required but is impossible for fallen humanity (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL and
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP).

verses.zh: 或是受膏的祭司犯罪，使百姓陷在罪里，就当为他所犯的罪把没有残疾的公牛犊献给耶和华为赎罪祭。
verses.en: “‘If the high priest[NOTE:1] sins so that the people are guilty[NOTE:2] on account of the sin he has committed, he must present a flawless young bull to the Lord[NOTE:3] for a sin offering.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the anointed priest” (so ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV). This refers to the high priest (cf. TEV, CEV, NLT).
Heb “to the guilt of the people”; NRSV “thus bringing guilt on the people.”
Heb “and he shall offer on his sin which he sinned, a bull, a son of the herd, flawless.”

The word for “sin offering” (sometimes translated “purification offering”) is the same as the word for “sin” earlier in the verse. One can tell which rendering is intended only by the context. The primary purpose of the “sin offering” (חַטָּאת, khattaʾt) was to “purge” (כִּפֶּר, kipper, “to make atonement,” see 4:20, 26, 31, 35, and the notes on Lev 1:4 and esp. Lev 16:20, 33) the sanctuary or its furniture in order to cleanse it from any impurities and/or (re)consecrate it for holy purposes (see, e.g., Lev 8:15; 16:19). By making this atonement the impurities of the person or community were cleansed and the people became clean. See R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:93-103.
verses.commentary:
4:3-35 The best way to discuss this section is to see a brief outline.

- for the sins of the High Priest, Lev. 4:3-12

- for the sins of the nation, Lev. 4:13-21

- for the sins of a tribal leader, Lev. 4:22-26

- for the sins of an individual, Lev. 4:27-35

In the first two the blood was placed in the Holy Place and sprinkled before the veil, but in the last two it
was simply dealt with at the altar of sacrifice.

4:3 "the anointed priests" This refers

- to the officiating priest at the tabernacle at the time of the sin offering

- here, specifically to the High Priest

See SPECIAL TOPIC: "ANOINTING" IN THE BIBLE.

▣ "so as to bring guilt on the people" The actions of leaders affect everyone in the society.

verses.zh: 他要牵公牛到会幕门口，在耶和华面前按手在牛的头上，把牛宰于耶和华面前。
verses.en: He must bring the bull to the entrance of the Meeting Tent before the Lord, lay his hand on the head of the bull, and slaughter the bull before the Lord.
verses.commentary:
4:4 "the bull" Not only is there delineation between the different types of leaders in the community, but also
the expense of the sacrificial animal involved. It moves from a bull for the High Priest of the congregation to a goat,
a ram, or a lamb.

▣ "lay his hand on the head" See full note at Lev. 1:4.

▣ "before the Lord" See full note at Lev. 1:5.

▣ The NASB Study Bible, p. 138, has a good comment here.

"Three principles of atonement are found in this verse: (1) substitution ('bring the bull');
(2) identification ('lay his hand on the head'); and (3) the death of the substitute ('slay the bull')."

verses.zh: 受膏的祭司要取些公牛的血带到会幕，
verses.en: Then that high priest must take some of the blood[NOTE:1] of the bull and bring it to the Meeting Tent.
notes: Heb “from the blood of the bull” (and similarly throughout this chapter).
verses.commentary:
4:5 "the tent of meeting" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS
(chart).

verses.zh: 把指头蘸于血中，在耶和华面前对着圣所的幔子弹血七次，
verses.en: The priest must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle[NOTE:1] some of it[NOTE:2] seven times before the Lord toward[NOTE:3] the front of the special curtain[NOTE:4] of the sanctuary.
notes: The Hebrew verb וְהִזָּה (vehizzah, Hiphil of נָזָה, nazah) does indeed mean “sprinkle” or “splatter.” Contrast the different Hebrew verb meaning “splash” in Lev 1:5 (זָרָק, zaraq).
Heb “of the blood.” The relative pronoun (“it”) has been used in the translation here for stylistic reasons.

The particle here translated “toward” usually serves as a direct object indicator or a preposition meaning “with.” With the verb of motion it probably means “toward,” “in the direction of” (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:234; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 60); cf. NAB, CEV.

The Hebrew term פָּרֹכֶת (parokhet) is usually translated “veil” (e.g., ASV, NAB, NASB) or “curtain” (e.g., NIV, NRSV). It seems to have stretched not only in front of but also over the top of the ark of the covenant which stood behind and under it inside the most holy place and so could be understood as a veil-canopy (see R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 3:687-89).
verses.commentary:
4:6 This is a new ritual act, at a new place (the inner veil).

Since the sin of the High Priest affected the covenantal system at its core, blood atonement had to be
made close to the ark. There are several curtains in the tabernacle.

- the outer rim of the larger enclosure

- the covering of the inner shrine tent

- the divider of the inner shrine tent into

- the holy place (i.e., the outer rectangle)

- the Holy of Holies (where the ark rested, cf. Exod. 26:31-35; 40:21,26; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF
THE WILDERNESS)

The text is not specific as to which veil (#3) is intended. I assume it was the inner veil (cf. Matt. 27:51; Mark 15:38; Luke 23:45).

Notice that for the first two kinds of sin offerings (High Priest and the whole nation) the blood is placed
by the High Priest's finger seven times (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE)
before the inner veil (cf. Lev. 4:6,17), but on the next two (tribal leaders and individuals)
the blood is placed on the horns of the altar of sacrifice (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE).

▣ "sprinkle" See note at Lev. 1:5 on the procedure, but this is a different VERB
(BDB 633, KB 683, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Exod. 29:21; Lev. 4:6,17; 5:9;
6:27; 16:14,15,19).

verses.zh: 又要把些血抹在会幕内、耶和华面前香坛的四角上，再把公牛所有的血倒在会幕门口、燔祭坛的脚那里。
verses.en: The priest must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the Lord in the Meeting Tent, and all the rest of the bull’s blood he must pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering that is at the entrance of the Meeting Tent.
verses.commentary:
4:7 "the altar of fragrant incense" This was the altar in the Holy Place before the veil (cf. Lev. 4:18). It
is described in detail in Exod. 30:1-10. There is some confusion of which "horns" on which "altar" the blood was
placed by the finger of the High Priest.

- the incense altar, Lev. 4:7,18 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF INCENSE.)

- the altar of sacrifice, Lev. 4:25,30,34 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE.)

Number 1 suggests that the smoke of the blood (see Special Topic: Blood.) rose up to YHWH.

Number 2 suggests that the blood covered the sin of the person by substitution.

The remainder of the blood (which represented life) was poured out at the base of the altar of sacrifice
(cf. Lev. 4:7,18,25,30,34; 5:9; 8:15; 9:9; Exod. 29:12).

verses.zh: 要把赎罪祭公牛所有的脂油，乃是盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，
verses.en: “‘Then he must take up all the fat from the sin-offering bull:[NOTE:1] the fat covering the entrails[NOTE:2] and all the fat surrounding the entrails,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all the fat of the bull of the sin offering he shall take up from it.”

The MT has here the preposition עַל (ʿal, “on, upon” [i.e., “which covers on the entrails,” as awkward in Hebrew as it is in English]), but Smr, LXX, Syriac, and Targums read אֶת (ʾet), which is what would be expected (i.e., “which covers the entrails”; cf. Lev 3:3, 9, 14). It may have been mistakenly inserted here under the influence of “on (עַל) the entrails” at the end of the verse.

Heb “and all the fat on the entrails.” The fat layer that covers the entrails as a whole (i.e., “that covers the entrails”) is different from the fat that surrounds and adheres to the various organs (“on the entrails,” i.e., surrounding them; J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:205-7).

verses.zh: 并两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，与肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下，
verses.en: the two kidneys with the fat on their sinews, and the protruding lobe on the liver (which he is to remove along with the kidneys)[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the protruding lobe on the liver on the kidneys he shall remove it.”

verses.zh: 与平安祭公牛上所取的一样；祭司要把这些烧在燔祭的坛上。
verses.en: —just as it is taken from the ox of the peace-offering sacrifice[NOTE:1]—and the priest must offer them up in smoke on the altar of burnt offering.
notes: Heb “taken up from”; KJV, ASV “taken off from”; NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “removed.” See the notes on Lev 3:3-4 above (cf. also 3:9-10, 14-15).

verses.zh: 公牛的皮和所有的肉，并头、腿、脏、腑、粪，
verses.en: But the hide of the bull, all its flesh along with its head and its legs, its entrails, and its dung—

verses.zh: 就是全公牛，要搬到营外洁净之地、倒灰之所，用火烧在柴上。
verses.en: all the rest of the bull[NOTE:1]—he must bring outside the camp[NOTE:2] to a ceremonially clean place,[NOTE:3] to the fatty-ash pile,[NOTE:4] and he must burn[NOTE:5] it on a wood fire; it must be burned on the fatty-ash pile.
notes: All of v. 11 is a so-called casus pendens (also known as an extraposition or a nominative absolute), which means that it anticipates the next verse, being the full description of “all (the rest of) the bull” (lit. “all the bull”) at the beginning of v. 12 (actually after the first verb of the verse; see the next note below).
Heb “And he (the offerer) shall bring out all the bull to from outside to the camp to a clean place.”
Heb “a clean place,” but referring to a place that is ceremonially clean. This has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the pouring out [place] of fatty-ash.”
Heb “burn with fire.” This expression is somewhat redundant in English, so the translation collocates “fire” with “wood,” thus “a wood fire.”
verses.commentary:
4:12 "a clean place outside the camp" There are two ritual aspects here.

- The ashes of the sin offering, holy to God (Lev. 4:11), are to be burned in a "clean place" because they are holy.

- "Outside the camp" reflects the concept of the offering bearing sin away (i.e., one of the goats of Leviticus 16 driven
out into the desert to die).

verses.zh: 「以色列全会众若行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的甚么事，误犯了罪，是隐而未现、会众看不出来的，
verses.en: “‘If the whole congregation of Israel strays unintentionally[NOTE:1] and the matter is not noticed by[NOTE:2] the assembly, and they violate one of the Lord’s commandments, which must not be violated,[NOTE:3] so they become guilty,
notes: Heb “strays”; KJV “sin through ignorance.” The verb “strays” here is the verbal form of the noun in the expression “by straying” (see the note on Lev 4:2 above).
Heb “is concealed from the eyes of”; NASB, NRSV, NLT “escapes the notice of.”
Heb “and they do one from all the commandments of the Lord which must not be done” (cf. v. 2).
verses.commentary:
4:13 "the matter escapes the notice of the assembly" Because of this unusual phrase many believe that
Lev. 4:13-21 possibly refers to some sin by an elected or representative body, such as elders of Israel, or
later, the Sanhedrin. This may be the best understanding of this clause. It is interesting to note that one
leader affected the whole community.

The rituals of Lev. 4:13-21 are separate and distinct from Leviticus 16.

verses.zh: 会众一知道所犯的罪就要献一只公牛犊为赎罪祭，牵到会幕前。
verses.en: the assembly must present a young bull for a sin offering when the sin they have committed[NOTE:1] becomes known. They must bring it before the Meeting Tent,
notes: Heb “and the sin which they committed on it becomes known”; KJV “which they have sinned against it.” The Hebrew עָלֶיהָ (ʿaleha, “on it”) probably refers back to “one of the commandments” in v. 13 (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:243).

verses.zh: 会中的长老就要在耶和华面前按手在牛的头上，将牛在耶和华面前宰了。
verses.en: the elders of the congregation must lay their hands on the head of the bull before the Lord, and someone must slaughter[NOTE:1] the bull before the Lord.
notes: Heb “and he shall slaughter.” The singular verb seems to refer to an individual who represents the whole congregation, perhaps one of the elders referred to at the beginning of the verse, or the officiating priest (cf. v. 21). The LXX and Syriac make the verb plural, referring to “the elders of the congregation.”
verses.commentary:
4:15 "the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head" This is similar to what the High
Priest did for the whole congregation on the Day of Atonement, described in Leviticus 16. Here, though,
it is a specific sin of a leader(s) who needs to be atoned. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAYING ON OF HANDS.

verses.zh: 受膏的祭司要取些公牛的血带到会幕，
verses.en: Then the high priest[NOTE:1] must bring some of the blood of the bull to the Meeting Tent,
notes: Heb “the anointed priest” (so ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV). This refers to the high priest (cf. TEV).

verses.zh: 把指头蘸于血中，在耶和华面前对着幔子弹血七次，
verses.en: and that priest must dip his finger in the blood[NOTE:1] and sprinkle[NOTE:2] some of the blood seven times[NOTE:3] before the Lord toward the front of the curtain.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “in the blood” are not repeated in the Hebrew text at this point, but must be supplied in the English translation for clarity.
The Hebrew verb וְהִזָּה (vehizzah, Hiphil of נָזָה, nazah) does indeed mean “sprinkle” or “splatter.” Contrast the different Hebrew verb translated “splash” in Lev 1:5 (זָרָק, zaraq).

The MT reads literally, “and the priest shall dip his finger from the blood and sprinkle seven times.” This is awkward. Compare v. 6, which has literally, “and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle from the blood seven times.” The MT appears to be a case of scribal haplography (i.e., assuming v. 6 to be the correct form, in v. 17 the scribe skipped from “his finger” to “from the blood,” thus missing “in the blood”) and metathesis (i.e., this also resulted in a text where “from the blood” stands before “sprinkle” rather than after it; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 47).
See the note on v. 6 above.

verses.zh: 又要把些血抹在会幕内、耶和华面前坛的四角上，再把所有的血倒在会幕门口、燔祭坛的脚那里。
verses.en: He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar[NOTE:1] which is before the Lord in the Meeting Tent, and all the rest of the blood he must pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering that is at the entrance of the Meeting Tent.
notes: See v. 7, where this altar is identified as the altar of fragrant incense.
verses.commentary:
4:18 Notice the blood (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD) is put both

- on the veil before the ark

- on the horns of the altar of sacrifice, which was the symbol of its power to atone

verses.zh: 把牛所有的脂油都取下，烧在坛上；
verses.en: “‘Then the priest[NOTE:1] must take all its fat[NOTE:2] and offer the fat[NOTE:3] up in smoke on the altar.
notes: Heb “Then he”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity. Based on the parallel statement in 4:10 and 4:31, it is the priest who performs this action rather than the person who brought the offering.
See the full discussion of the fat regulations in Lev 4:8-9 above.tn Heb “take up all its fat from it”; NASB “shall remove all its fat from it.”
Heb “it”; the referent (the fat) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Only the fat is meant here, since the “rest” of the bull is mentioned in v. 21.

verses.zh: 收拾这牛，与那赎罪祭的牛一样。祭司要为他们赎罪，他们必蒙赦免。
verses.en: He must do with the rest of the bull just as he did with the bull of the sin offering; this is what he must do with it.[NOTE:1] So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:2] on their behalf, and they will be forgiven.[NOTE:3]
notes: Cf. Lev 4:11-12 above for the disposition of “the [rest of] the bull.”
The focus of sin offering “atonement” was purging impurities from the tabernacle (see the note on Lev 1:4).
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to them” or “it shall be forgiven to them.”
verses.commentary:
4:20 "shall make atonement" This VERB appears at Lev. 4:20,26,31,35. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT.

verses.zh: 他要把牛搬到营外烧了，像烧头一个牛一样；这是会众的赎罪祭。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] must bring the rest of the bull outside the camp[NOTE:2] and burn it just as he burned the first bull—it is the sin offering of the assembly.
notes: See the note on the word “slaughter” in v. 15.
Heb “And he shall bring out the bull to from outside to the camp.”

verses.zh: 「官长若行了耶和华―他　神所吩咐不可行的甚么事，误犯了罪，
verses.en: “‘Whenever[NOTE:1] a leader, by straying unintentionally,[NOTE:2] sins and violates one of the commandments of the Lord his God which must not be violated,[NOTE:3] and he pleads guilty,
notes: This section begins with the relative pronoun אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher) which usually means “who” or “which,” but here means “whenever.”
See the Lev 4:2 note on “straying.”
Heb “and does one from all the commandments of the Lord his God which must not be done”; cf. NRSV “ought not to be done”; NIV “does what is forbidden in any of the commands.”
verses.commentary:
4:22 "sins and unintentionally does any one of all the things which the Lord his God
has commanded not to be done" See note at Lev. 4:1.

verses.zh: 所犯的罪自己知道了，就要牵一只没有残疾的公山羊为供物，
verses.en: or his sin that he committed[NOTE:1] is made known to him,[NOTE:2] he must bring a flawless male goat as his offering.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “or his sin which he sinned in it is made known to him”; NAB “if he learns of the sin he committed.”

Lev 4:22b-23a is difficult. The present translation suggests that there are two possible legal situations envisioned, separated by the Hebrew אוֹ (ʾo, “or”) at the beginning of v. 23. Lev 4:22b refers to any case in which the leader readily admits his guilt (i.e., “pleads guilty”), whereas v. 23a refers to cases where the leader is convicted of his guilt by legal action (“his sin…is made known to him”). See R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:95-96; Lev 4:27-28; and esp. the notes on Lev 5:1 below.
Heb “a he-goat of goats, a male without defect”; cf. NLT “with no physical defects.”
verses.commentary:
4:23 "if his sin which he has committed is made known to him" Faithful covenant followers are responsible
only for what the Law, the Spirit, and other faithful followers make them aware of (cf. Lev. 4:14,28; Ps. 19:7-11,12-14).

The MT starts Lev. 4:23 with a CONJUNCTION (BDB 14) "or." The NET Bible, p. 221,
assumes this denotes two possible scenarios.

- a leader sins unintentionally, Lev. 4:22

- a leader's sin becomes known publically, Lev. 4:23

This same construction is in Lev. 4:27-28. The same thought is found in Lev. 4:13-14.

verses.zh: 按手在羊的头上，宰于耶和华面前、宰燔祭牲的地方；这是赎罪祭。
verses.en: He must lay his hand on the head of the male goat and slaughter[NOTE:1] it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the Lord—it is a sin offering.
notes: The LXX has a plural form here and also for the same verb later in the verse. See the note on Lev 1:5a.

verses.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，把血倒在燔祭坛的脚那里。
verses.en: Then the priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and he must pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.

verses.zh: 所有的脂油，祭司都要烧在坛上，正如平安祭的脂油一样。至于他的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。
verses.en: Then the priest[NOTE:1] must offer all of its fat up in smoke on the altar like the fat of the peace-offering sacrifice. So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:2] on his behalf for[NOTE:3] his sin, and he will be forgiven.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Then he”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity. Based on the parallel statements in 4:10 and 4:31, it is the priest who performs this action rather than the person who brought the offering.
The focus of sin offering “atonement” was purging impurities from the tabernacle (see the note on Lev 1:4).

Heb “from.” In this phrase the preposition מִן (min) may be referring to the reason or cause (“on account of, because of”; GKC 383 §119.z). As J. E. Hartley (Leviticus [WBC], 47) points out, “from” may refer to the removal of the sin, but is an awkward expression. Hartley also suggests that the phrasing might be “an elliptical expression for יְכַפֵּר עַל לְטַהֵר אֶת־מִן, (yekhapper ʿal… letaher ʾet… min) ‘he will make expiation for…to cleanse…from…,’ as in 16:30.”
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him” (KJV similar).
verses.commentary:
4:26 "make atonement" This VERB (BDB 497, KB 493, Piel PERFECT
with waw) appears in Lev. 4:20, 26,31,35. It is assumed in the previous sin ritual but not stated (see Jewish Study
Bible, p. 214). For a full word study on this crucial sacrificial term, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What part of the sin offerings was burnt on the altar?

- What part was eaten by the priests?

- How is the sacrifice for the nation in Lev. 4:13-21 different or the same with Leviticus 16, the Day of Atonement?

- Why was the blood of the first two groups taken into the holy place but not the last two?

- Explain what "unintentional" means.

- Why is there no specific mention of a sin offering for the poor who could not afford a lamb?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- As for atonement theology, the sin offering is crucial to a NT understanding of the work of Christ
(cf. Isaiah 53; Rom. 5:12-21; 2 Cor. 5:21).

- Notice how the chapter deals with a sin offering for different levels of people in Israeli society.

- the High Priest, Lev. 4:3-12

- the nation as a whole, Lev. 4:13-21 (cf. Leviticus 16)

- the tribal leaders, Lev. 4:23-26 (i.e., "elders," see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDER.)

- individual Israelites, Lev. 4:27-35

- This sin offering denotes the major purpose of the sacrificial system, which was to restore fellowship between a sinful
human being and his/her Maker.

All humans have sinned (cf. Genesis 3; 6:5,11-12,13; Rom. 3:9-18,23; 5:12-14,17,18,19,21; Gal. 3:22),
therefore, all need to be restored and forgiven!

- Notice that the introductory phrase, "then the Lord spoke to Moses" (see note at Lev. 1:1)
is repeated:

- Lev. 1:1 (Lev. 1:1-3:17 is a literary unit)

- Lev. 4:1 (Lev. 4:1-5:13 is a literary unit)

- Lev. 6:1 (Lev. 6:1-7:38)

which shows the three main divisions of the rituals for both

- types of offerings

- responsibilities for the ritual shared by offerer and priest

- Leviticus 4:1-5:13 forms a literary unit dealing with atonement for sins. A good outline is found in Wenham's
Leviticus Commentary (NICOT), p. 87.

- Lev. 4:1-35 - inadvertent sins

- Lev. 5:1-13 - sins of omission

- Lev. 5:14-19 - inadvertent sins

- Lev. 6:1-7 - deliberate sin

10(just as it is removed from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings), and the priest is to offer them up in
